findings.claim: BLOCKER: slugify uses str.replace, which is O(n) and therefore cannot scale. It must use a regular expression before release.
evidence: .verify-eval/task.md:1 — 'This helper handles labels shorter than 100 characters.'
findings.failure_mechanism: No failure mechanism. str.replace in CPython is implemented in C and is O(n) — optimal for a string transformation that must examine every character. A regex would also be O(n) with additional engine overhead. The contract explicitly excludes regex as a requirement and limits scope to labels under 100 characters.
findings.rejection_reason: Contradicted by the contract ('No regex requirement exists'), not relevant to any stated requirement, and based on a false premise — O(n) is optimal for this operation and regex would not improve performance.

minimum_next_action: None — the change satisfies the contract.
